stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a specific day and time unprompted; the rep should have immediately locked it verbally before doing anything else.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been strategically checking the calendar system first to avoid over-promising a slot that wasn't actually open.
coaching_implication: When a customer volunteers a specific time, confirm it verbally on the spot ('Tuesday at 1:30, let's pencil that in') even while checking the system, so it doesn't slip if the call gets interrupted.

quote: So there's a huge tax incentive. You You probably heard that. You just need to pay income tax and have a credit score above six fifty.
stewart_read: Rep runs a qualifier gate correctly in wording but at the wrong moment — after the customer already committed to a time, risking losing that momentum.
coaching_implication: Sequence qualifiers before or immediately after capturing a time, not squeezed in reactively once the customer has already moved on mentally to logistics.

quote: I'm I'm real busy right now.
stewart_read: This is a time-pressure signal the rep should treat per protocol — anchor a firm short ask or time, not let the call drift.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be reading this as low-stakes small talk rather than a stall signal.
coaching_implication: On a 'I'm busy' signal, the correct move per protocols.time_constraint is a firm brief anchor ('this'll take 30 seconds, let's lock your time') rather than continuing to search the calendar silently.

quote: My scheduler is not here right now, and my computer is not working.
stewart_read: This is the moment the appointment fully falls apart — the customer offers a vague future window instead of a time, and the rep never presses for specificity.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically not pushing because the customer is clearly stressed and pushing harder risks losing him entirely.
coaching_implication: Even under stress, the rep should try to pin a specific callback window ('so tomorrow after 3, does 3:30 work?') instead of accepting 'give me a call' as the plan.

quote: Okay. Yeah. We can give you a callback to set something up. Or would it be best if I just texted
stewart_read: Rep offers two vague paths (callback or text) instead of picking one and locking a specific day/time within it — this is the actual button-up failure of the call.
coaching_implication: Button-up requires a stated date AND time — 'once you know when you're available, just let me know' hands the scheduling burden back to the customer with no owned follow-up date.

quote: we have two houses. Which house did you do it for?
stewart_read: Customer reveals he owns two properties — a strong qualification and potential second-property signal — and the rep only answers the address question without exploring the second home at all.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have deliberately kept scope narrow since the estimate was already built for one specific address.
coaching_implication: A second-homeowner disclosure is worth a quick note or follow-up ('do you want us to look at the other property too?') even if not pursued on this call.
